fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Why the Priest Class Always Got Time Wrong", "body": "Asked about the vast time cycles the priest class has handed down, Dylan argues its calendar keepers have always been wrong, because the cycles move so gradually that they can only be worked out by calculation from records that were never perfect. He says the Vatican takes its name from the vates, the seer, and ties bishops to the astronomers who told farmers when to plant, since no empire thrived without starchy grain. The Chaldeans, he says, came closest, and the calendar corrected in Caesar's era held for nearly fifteen hundred years before the Gregorian fix. Stretching the cycles, he contends, was how priesthoods passed themselves off as ancient."}, {"title": "Cataclysm, Mud Floods and a Broken Strait", "body": "When Dylan turns the question around and asks whether the year was ever a tidy 360 days, Chance says he does not know and calls it a big assumption to think anyone does, though he suspects some huge cataclysmic trauma in humanity's past. His favorite trail is an electrolysis type event in the larger battery of this realm that literally added land, with the mud flood as new earth and Ragnarok as a recharge. Dylan answers with his own shoreline, unchanged in thirty years, and wonders whether the Strait of Gibraltar was once a land bridge the Atlantic broke through, while insisting there is no evidence for Atlantis."}, {"title": "Sanskrit and the Priestly Languages", "body": "Previewing his fifth book, Dylan argues that the Irish used the same seventeen letters the Phoenicians gave the Greeks and that Welsh is comparable to Hebrew. He treats Sanskrit, which shares more than thirty words with Latin and Irish, as the only language formed by rule and preserved by priests, with Etruscan coming from that source and Latin a corruption of Etruscan. Spoken dialects, he says, are just people conveying their needs, while written languages are priestly systems, which is why he calls Hebrew a Masonic language and counts Hebrew and Arabic as learned tongues that nobody spoke until they were made common in the Middle Ages."}, {"title": "From Java to Oaxaca", "body": "Dylan's fifth book aims to show the ancient world knew the Americas, starting with Mexico, whose calendar shared Egypt's 360 days plus five dead days, and whose people spoke what the Jesuits called a corrupt Hebrew without letters, which he argues rules out a European import. He then looks to Java: an Arabic writer described an island in the China Sea so rich in gold its dogs wore golden chains, and centuries later a Portuguese apothecary wrote of Javanese hounds with gold and silver collars. He hears Oaxaca in that island's name, and suspects the Americans were called Indians because older maritime empires knew they came from India."}, {"title": "Bridge Builders Who Became Gatekeepers", "body": "Dylan calls the Javanese sailors and bridge builders, since a brig is a bridge, and follows the word to the pontifex, with the pope as the greatest bridge builder. A bridge sits between two things, and he argues the middleman turns parasitic once it stops being a bridge and becomes a gatekeeper, from the church to merchants skimming profits, the mob, the unions and Hollywood. To leave the system, he says, you must look at the priest system it comes from. Chance's closing takes the same line: the aim is not to crush anyone's spirituality but to strip out the dogma that makes people subservient to middlemen."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dylan Saccoccio returns to InnerVerse to present material from his fourth Spirit Whirled book, A God's Acre for Winds of the Soul, and the research that will become book five.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this session: Dylan's case that all written languages descend from a single source, how he reads Sanskrit, Latin, Irish Gaelic, Welsh, and Hebrew as dialects of the same priestly system, how the calendar corrected under Caesar held for nearly 1,500 years before the Gregorian fix, how, in his view, priest classes across cultures used inflated time cycles to appear older than they were, Buddha and Thoth and Hermes and Mercury as different names for the same solar archetype, the Javanese sailors as the original Pontifical bridge builders, and whether the Vatican is named after the Etruscan goddess Vatica.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Orient, Occident and the Irish Question", "body": "The members hour opens on a split between the Orient, which represents things with characters, and the Occident, which uses letters to signify sounds, two different ways of thinking that Dylan says feed into the Irish ogham. He rejects the popular claim that civilization and language began in Ireland, went to India and came back, resting his objection on climate and on the symbolism buried in the language itself, since the skies over Britain stay cloudy most of the year and would make that depth of astronomy far slower to acquire. He still holds the door open, saying he preserves his right to change his opinion."}, {"title": "Rome, Etruria and the Sardinian Thread", "body": "Much of the exclusive hour circles back to Italy. Dylan reads the first three hundred years of Rome as observable astrotheology and points out that the first king, Numa, becomes a moon when his name is read like Hebrew. He treats the Etruscans and the Phoenicians as inseparable on linguistic grounds, since Phoenician tablets turn up in Tuscany, and he sends listeners to the Monte Prama discoveries in Sardinia, explaining the sardonic laugh as the grimace left by a Phoenician hemlock poison. He also insists the Druids were the priests of Apollo and the fathers of the church, which is why Caesar kept close company with them."}, {"title": "The Secret Letters of Leaves", "body": "The richest thread of the hour is what Dylan calls the secret letters of leaves. He traces early Greek letters, said to be formed of straight lines and later called petala or leaves, into the druidic and Irish system where the letters carry tree names, and on to Hebrew letters named for trees as well. Beech bark carried the writing, which is how beech becomes book, and the rolled bark called liber is why we still count things in volumes. Rana means frog, named for the small green frogs singing in the beech trees, and that, he argues, is the root of green language."}, {"title": "Numbers as the Universal Character", "body": "Dylan's throughline is that the oldest written language was numerical and that numbers function as a universal character. He reads an account of the Chinese written language being understood from the Russian border through Korea, Japan, Malacca and Java by populations who cannot speak to one another at all, and sets it beside Roman numerals to argue for an old language of commerce carried by a maritime empire. Twenty letters, he notes, are enough to convey ten thousand words, so every nation can keep its own tongue and still be understood. Once shared words reach eight, he puts the odds against coincidence at eight hundred thousand to one."}, {"title": "Defeating the Presumption", "body": "The philosophical spine of the exclusive material is Dylan's insistence that the mystery school figures were never historical people. He asks how many works Socrates, Jesus or Muhammad left behind, answers zero, and argues that once you see how old the system is and how it ties every culture together you can defeat the presumption of anyone claiming authority by descent from Noah or Japheth. Chance, who reads the work as a practitioner, calls the whole benefit of syncretism the moment you start seeing an almost universality in language. Dylan describes realizing it was all allegory, which he found far more empowering than the history he was handed."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "As information available in the system goes up, attention spans go down.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "How many works did Socrates leave behind, how many works did Jesus leave behind, how many works did Muhammad leave behind?", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It's not reality if it's only something that you can imagine.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "This ultimately ties back to why everything's named after trees and leaves because they wrote on branches.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The whole benefit of syncretism is that you do start to see this almost universality in language.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Once you can defeat the presumption, you take your power back and you stop genuflecting to these freaks who are using lies to enslave you.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The Druids are the priests of Apollo. They are the fathers of the church.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Every nation can retain its own language yet understand each other without learning or speaking each other's dialects.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You can change everything, but your language will betray you.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Bringing attention to the problem allows energy to flow to the thing and nature to do the self-correcting mechanisms that it innately does.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "All language is the same. It's just different people trying to convey their ideas of what they need.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I find that when I spend the time doing what's best for my health and taking the time to do that, I feel like I have more time throughout the rest of the day.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It gets to a point where history is so defiled by mythology that you can't separate the two.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "There's not one hieroglyphic on the three Great Pyramids. So what you're seeing is an older civilization.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Every Mason was a priest but not every priest was a mason.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We're not really here to crush people's spirituality or the value in some of these ancient mystery school traditions that have passed forward into today in the form of Christianity.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It's really interesting how cultures who have no connection to each other could share the exact same astronomical mistakes.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If we want to get out of the system and remove its authority, we have to be willing to look at the priest system that it comes from.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
